string-array.name: journey_facts
string-array.item: Everyone starts from here. The first stop is Cremona, where the violin was invented.
Amati, Stradivari and Guarneri worked here — the violin as we know it was invented in this city.
The theatre opened in 1778; operas by Verdi and Puccini\'s “Madama Butterfly” were first heard here.
Mozart was born here; Hohensalzburg Fortress has stood above the city since the 11th century.
Every year on 1 January the New Year\'s Concert goes out from here to the whole world. The hall is counted among the finest for acoustics.
Dvořák conducted the first concert of the Czech Philharmonic here.
Bach was cantor of St Thomas Church for a quarter of a century.
A “tent” of a hall, where the stage stands in the middle of the audience.
The orchestra of the hall bears the title “Royal”.
Opened in 1875; the ceiling of the auditorium was painted by Marc Chagall in 1964.
Opened in 1871; the Proms are held here every summer.
Here, in August 1942, during the siege, Shostakovich\'s Seventh Symphony was performed.
Opened in 1901; the Tchaikovsky Competition is held here.
“How do you get to Carnegie Hall? — Practice.”
Opened in 1908 with “Aida”; its acoustics are called some of the best in the world.
A “vineyard” hall: the audience sits in terraces around the stage. Opened in 1986.
Under the “sails” there are several halls; the silhouette is known even to those who have never been to Australia.
